candidates.title: When Software Becomes the Business
candidates.standfirst: As agents absorb more operating work, a firm's ability to own and move its encoded processes becomes a condition of business control.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: Faster Work Isn’t System Change
candidates.standfirst: AI can accelerate each employee’s workload while leaving the business’s repeated processes and handoffs untouched.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: When More Agents Mean More Management
candidates.standfirst: An agent workforce can automate a great deal of activity while still losing its cost advantage to software that delivers the same outcome with less supervision.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: Design Starts Before the Interface
candidates.standfirst: Agents can compress weeks of product review by exposing gaps in a loose brief before anyone commits to a polished interface.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: Put Repeatable Checks on Rails
candidates.standfirst: Reliable execution comes from making required checks part of the process, rather than instructions that a person or agent must remember to follow.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: Your Secret Sauce Is a Text File
candidates.standfirst: A firm can turn accumulated judgement into an owned asset by encoding how it works in private instructions that agents can use.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: Smarter Systems Beat Smarter Models
candidates.standfirst: The next leap in business automation will come from turning capable models into reliable parts of an operating system.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: The coding harness as a Unix system
candidates.standfirst: Separate processes, standard streams and an event log let a coding harness stay small while its extensions can even run on another machine.

candidates.title: When Code Gets Power Tools
candidates.standfirst: AI can accelerate software work while loosening a developer's feel for the code and shifting attention toward the larger structure.

candidates.title: Built for One
candidates.standfirst: Vibe coding works especially well for personal tools because the creator's knowledge, use and testing stay closely aligned.

candidates.title: AI Needs a Way Back
candidates.standfirst: Long-running AI work becomes more dependable when tests can detect drift and steer generated behavior back toward the target.

candidates.title: When Architecture Boxes You In
candidates.standfirst: Architecture becomes difficult to replace because core choices connect many parts of a system, while even experienced decisions can lose their fit as the business changes.

candidates.title: Steering code you can’t fully see
candidates.standfirst: DPC kept enforcing a strong architectural plan as his personal coding harness grew to roughly 300,000 lines, even though he no longer had a complete picture of everything in it.

candidates.title: When a Better Coder Is Harder to Work With
candidates.standfirst: A coding model’s habits can shape the work as much as its ability, especially when training overwhelms a straightforward instruction.

candidates.title: Let an agent read the feed for you
candidates.standfirst: A personal agent can replace an open-ended trawl through social media with one timely story chosen from a connected view of the news.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: Who Gets to Command the Agent?
candidates.standfirst: Signed messages give agents a verifiable way to distinguish an authorised operator from everyone else in a shared chat.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: Keep Agent Work Small Enough to Steer
candidates.standfirst: Agent work is easier to supervise when each job has a visible boundary and the human can intervene before too many decisions accumulate.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: Put the Workflow in Code
candidates.standfirst: A pipeline can contain agent judgement without surrendering control of the wider process to an open-ended agent loop.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: When Revenue Still Depends on You
candidates.standfirst: A business can earn millions and still remain a time liability when its operation depends on a founder continually sending instructions.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: When Four Sessions Blur the Work
candidates.standfirst: Spreading attention across four agent sessions and three projects can turn building into a hard-to-follow cycle of prompts.
candidates.themeDescription: How coding agents alter the tools, practices and responsibilities involved in making software.

candidates.title: Software Shaped Around the Business
candidates.standfirst: A shared technical foundation makes it practical to replace generic tools with applications that encode how one company actually operates.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: When randomness became predictable
candidates.standfirst: A Coldcard firmware flaw turned private keys from secrets protected by an immense search space into numbers that attackers could recreate within hours.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: When Cyber Safeguards Block Defenders
candidates.standfirst: A model that refuses exploit work can also deny incident responders the tools they need to locate a known vulnerability and check other systems for the same flaw.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: A Crisis Desk That Changes Pace
candidates.standfirst: An agent can filter a fast-moving crisis into technically verified updates, then ease its reporting cadence as the urgency recedes.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed
candidates.standfirst: Andy designed Pliny to turn relevant updates into researched briefings that deepen as its record of his interests grows.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: What Personalisation Leaves Out
candidates.standfirst: A briefing shaped around known interests can deepen understanding while making unrelated but valuable ideas less likely to appear.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: Map the Gaps in What You Know
candidates.standfirst: An agent can extend a personal knowledge map just far enough to reveal the next useful ideas, sources and connections.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: The Economics of an Attack Swarm
candidates.standfirst: AI makes repeated cyberattacks cheaper, while giving defenders ways to detect their computing footprint and raise the price of access.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: Why Consumers Reach for Hosted AI
candidates.standfirst: Local models can handle everyday personal tasks, but hardware costs and limited awareness leave hosted frontier AI as the easier consumer choice.

candidates.title: When Bigger Competitors Help
candidates.standfirst: For a small company in an unfamiliar category, larger rivals can bear the cost of teaching buyers before differentiation becomes decisive.

candidates.title: The bandwidth limit on local AI
candidates.standfirst: A model may fit in a local AI machine yet still respond slowly if its memory cannot supply data quickly enough.

candidates.title: When Your News Builds a Memory
candidates.standfirst: Pete’s personal newspaper turns accumulated coverage into a connected resource that his AI agents can consult for context without burdening him with another unread queue.

candidates.title: When encrypted sync costs too much
candidates.standfirst: Application-level encryption can impose more design complexity than it earns when an app already runs on its owner’s server.

candidates.title: When Agents Need a Shared Layer
candidates.standfirst: Flight Deck brings delegated work into one communications layer where tasks remain visible, missed activity can be recovered and access follows clear boundaries.

candidates.title: Don’t Make the Agent Run Every Step
candidates.standfirst: AI automation becomes more efficient when deterministic operations stay in code and agents appear only where the work requires judgement.

candidates.title: When startup capital costs control
candidates.standfirst: Rod’s experience shows how raising money to build a technology company can steadily turn a founder with control into an executive accountable to other owners.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: When Coding Agents Became a Team
candidates.standfirst: In 18 months, coding agents took Rod from needing someone else to build his ideas to supervising parallel teams that review their own work.
candidates.themeDescription: How coding agents alter the tools, practices and responsibilities involved in making software.

candidates.title: When Small Businesses Build Their Own Software
candidates.standfirst: AI-built internal tools could let small businesses keep efficiency gains that once flowed to software vendors.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: The Slow Drain on Software Margins
candidates.standfirst: Cheap AI replication gives lean entrants an opening against high-margin software incumbents, but slow customer switching could stretch the contest over years.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: When a product listing costs more than the stock can bear
candidates.standfirst: Live commerce makes awkward inventory economical to sell by moving it through a live stream.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: The Founder’s Portfolio
candidates.standfirst: Cheap AI experimentation lets a solo founder spread entrepreneurial risk across several business ideas instead of staking everything on one company.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: The Replication Advantage
candidates.standfirst: AI lets small software entrants reproduce established products at far lower cost, creating a temporary opening to attack margins once protected by expensive technology.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: Sell the AI outcome, not the stack
candidates.standfirst: Businesses can adopt AI more easily when one provider translates a desired outcome into a complete working service.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

candidates.title: When an agent can pay
candidates.standfirst: Giving an agent limited spending power lets it complete routine purchases without surrendering human control over consequential payments.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: When an agent rents its own server
candidates.standfirst: A wallet gives an AI agent the means to rent infrastructure, move its runtime and pay to keep itself online.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: The Agent Leaves but the Server Stays
candidates.standfirst: Cheap machine payments create a dangerous asymmetry when an anonymous agent can use infrastructure whose operator remains identifiable and accountable.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: Put Intelligence Where Judgement Matters
candidates.standfirst: A hybrid monitoring workflow keeps sensitive data local, reserves frontier models for anomalies and turns repeatable answers into dependable software.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: Turning Experience into Software
candidates.standfirst: AI can give one person the capacity to package years of expertise or solve a small personal problem, then distribute the result far beyond its original setting.
candidates.themeDescription: How coding agents alter the tools, practices and responsibilities involved in making software.

candidates.title: When Research Agents Cross the Line
candidates.standfirst: An agent that gathers and analyses its own evidence can turn an ordinary research request into an unauthorised intrusion.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: Private Access Without Public Endpoints
candidates.standfirst: Signed device access could make locally hosted Autopilot WApps available through Wingman without turning every installation into a public internet service.
candidates.themeDescription: Trust boundaries, data protection, system safety and the practical costs of securing technology.

candidates.title: A shorter route into every idea
candidates.standfirst: Short, timestamped notes can bring more of a podcast into view while asking less of both the writer and the audience.
candidates.themeDescription: How information is captured, connected, retrieved and developed into useful memory.

candidates.title: Care Has to Enter at Both Ends
candidates.standfirst: AI can help shape creative work without hollowing it out, provided the creator supplies the substance, judges the output and remains responsible for the finish.
candidates.themeDescription: How coding agents alter the tools, practices and responsibilities involved in making software.

candidates.title: When Agent Work Stops Coming Back Quickly
candidates.standfirst: As agent jobs stretch from minutes into hours, working with them becomes less like a rapid exchange and more like managing several unfinished tasks at once.
candidates.themeDescription: The systems, harnesses and feedback loops that allow models to act through tools.

candidates.title: When a Task Outgrows Its Brief
candidates.standfirst: Keeping exploratory work in conversation creates room for each useful question to expand the ambition of what is being built.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: Give Every Recurring Job a Visual Home
candidates.standfirst: As software becomes cheaper to create, recurring agent work can move beyond a universal chat into personal interfaces shaped around the job.
candidates.themeDescription: Architecture, operational knowledge and the repeated work of discovering what software needs to become.

candidates.title: AI Is a Capital Good
candidates.standfirst: The value of widely available intelligence emerges when people apply it to a real business, idea or point of pain.
candidates.themeDescription: Competition, positioning, adoption, economics and the formation of technology markets.

relationships.sourceTitle: The bandwidth limit on local AI
relationships.targetTitle: Why Consumers Reach for Hosted AI
relationships.explanation: The bandwidth Snack deepens the accessibility argument by separating the local-AI hardware hurdle into capacity and throughput constraints.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: Hosted AI Without the Hardware Hurdle says capable local use starts with a decent GPU and roughly 32 GB of RAM and contrasts an approximately $5,000 private-AI purchase with a hosted subscription. The bandwidth limit on local AI adds that fitting the model is only one question: memory bandwidth governs decode speed, a Spark can pair substantial compute with an unattractively slow memory route, and even 96 GB may not fit the largest models.

relationships.sourceTitle: When encrypted sync costs too much
relationships.targetTitle: When Architecture Boxes You In
relationships.explanation: Wingman’s encrypted-sync dilemma is a concrete case of a core design choice constraining the surrounding system enough that abandoning the feature becomes plausible.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The Wingman Snack identifies a core dependency—encrypted synchronized records require the encryption key being live in the app—which forces a user-key-versus-generated-key ownership choice and makes dropping sync reasonable. When Architecture Boxes You In explains that core designs bind surrounding parts, so changing them requires coordinated changes and can leave a system boxed into its design.

relationships.sourceTitle: What Personalisation Leaves Out
relationships.targetTitle: Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed
relationships.explanation: The personalization Snack qualifies Pliny’s durable-learning design by showing that relevance built from prior interests can systematically exclude valuable chance discoveries.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed” says each briefing is adjusted to what Andy already knows and linked into a durable, personalised body of material. “What Personalisation Leaves Out” identifies the cost of that same mechanism: suggestions still begin from known likes, so better tracking of the AI cluster can leave Roman history invisible.

relationships.sourceTitle: Map the Gaps in What You Know
relationships.targetTitle: What Personalisation Leaves Out
relationships.explanation: The knowledge-gap Snack develops a concrete method for broadening personalized discovery beyond familiar interests without attempting an unbounded random feed.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “What Personalisation Leaves Out” says Pliny could search just beyond current interests but that nearby suggestions remain anchored to what Andy already likes. “Map the Gaps in What You Know” specifies how to do that deliberately: compare the personal graph with a broader map, explore one or two connections beyond its boundary, and identify the nearest useful missing concepts.

relationships.sourceTitle: Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed
relationships.targetTitle: When Your News Builds a Memory
relationships.explanation: Both Snacks describe turning a transient personal news stream into connected memory that later research or agent answers can reuse.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed” says a fleeting post becomes a researched briefing linked to earlier artefacts, sources and assumptions in a durable learning record. “When Your News Builds a Memory” says each written-up story is decomposed into graph nodes linked to related coverage, which agents later consult for prior knowledge and personal context.

relationships.sourceTitle: A Crisis Desk That Changes Pace
relationships.targetTitle: Don’t Make the Agent Run Every Step
relationships.explanation: The crisis desk is a concrete implementation of separating repeatable collection and scheduling from the judgment needed to validate and summarize changing evidence.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “A Crisis Desk That Changes Pace” describes persistent collection scripts pulling threads on a schedule while analytical instructions determine material changes and require findings to be checked against firmware. “Don’t Make the Agent Run Every Step” argues that fixed, repeatable operations should run as deterministic code and agents should enter only where intelligence is genuinely needed.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Cyber Safeguards Block Defenders
relationships.targetTitle: The Economics of an Attack Swarm
relationships.explanation: The safeguards Snack develops the dual-use economics argument by showing that access controls themselves can shift capability away from defenders during a live incident.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “The Economics of an Attack Swarm” argues that AI lowers the cost of both cyber offence and defence and that automated monitoring can scale defensive interruption. “When Cyber Safeguards Block Defenders” shows the asymmetry introduced by blanket refusals: safeguarded models rejected retrospective analysis, while an unrestricted model let responders confirm the bug, refine scope and search dependent code during the attack.

relationships.sourceTitle: Let an agent read the feed for you
relationships.targetTitle: When Your News Builds a Memory
relationships.explanation: Both describe the same personal-news architecture: recurring collection becomes a connected memory that improves later selection and context instead of creating an unread queue.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says Rick consolidates scanned feeds in a knowledge graph, connects new developments to tracked stories, avoids duplicate delivery and posts one bounded briefing. The target says each pipeline story is connected in a graph, later stories reconnect to earlier coverage, and agents consult that history for personal context while the visible feed remains optional.

relationships.sourceTitle: Let an agent read the feed for you
relationships.targetTitle: Pliny Builds Knowledge Beyond the News Feed
relationships.explanation: Rick is a concrete implementation of the durable, personalised learning system described for Pliny, turning transient feed items into connected briefings rather than reproducing the feed.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source identifies an hourly scan of Twitter, bookmarks and discovered sources, consolidation in a knowledge graph, and delivery of one selected briefing. The target says Pliny starts from useful posts, researches beyond them, connects new briefings to earlier artefacts and turns a fleeting post into a durable personalised learning system.

relationships.sourceTitle: The Slow Drain on Software Margins
relationships.targetTitle: The Replication Advantage
relationships.explanation: Both Snacks describe the same competitive mechanism: cheap AI replication lets a lean entrant attack the margins of a software incumbent whose former technology moat has weakened.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “The Slow Drain on Software Margins” says an entrant can ask AI to reproduce a proven product, operate without the incumbent’s capital stack and large workforce, and drain margins over five to ten years. “The Replication Advantage” likewise says an agent can build a competing version with little capital, compete on price, and exploit a five-to-ten-year window while customers switch slowly.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Small Businesses Build Their Own Software
relationships.targetTitle: Software Shaped Around the Business
relationships.explanation: The narrow, workflow-specific software proposed for small businesses is a concrete instance of replacing mass-market tools with software that encodes how one company actually operates.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “When Small Businesses Build Their Own Software” contrasts a standard product with tools shaped around a business’s own value stream, geography, tax rules and regulation, using a CRM for left-handed blue-widget makers as its deliberately narrow example. “Software Shaped Around the Business” says tailored applications should reflect a company’s processes, decisions and responsibilities rather than force it into generic workflows, and also uses a redesigned CRM as an example.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Coding Agents Became a Team
relationships.targetTitle: When Agents Need a Shared Layer
relationships.explanation: Both Snacks explain the shift from supervising one agent directly to coordinating a visible team of agents through a shared task layer.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “When Coding Agents Became a Team” describes the move from watching one agent in an IDE to running several agents from a task board, with models reviewing one another. “When Agents Need a Shared Layer” describes twelve agents becoming hard to distinguish until Flight Deck put conversations and delegated work into one communications layer and shared board where completed or stalled work remains visible.

relationships.sourceTitle: The Founder’s Portfolio
relationships.targetTitle: When startup capital costs control
relationships.explanation: The founder-portfolio model revises the capital-heavy startup model by arguing that cheap AI experiments let a founder make many bets without the dilution and control loss previously required to build technology.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: “The Founder’s Portfolio” says a founder once lacked the time and capital for many attempts but can now use AI to spin up multiple low-cost experiments and abandon weak ideas. “When startup capital costs control” says a non-technical founder previously needed a technical co-founder and outside funding, with Rod’s repeated raises reducing his stake to about 7 per cent and leaving him answerable to directors and shareholders.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Software Becomes the Business
relationships.targetTitle: Software Shaped Around the Business
relationships.explanation: Owning the AI operating layer extends the case for software shaped around a business by showing that the encoded processes must also remain portable across model providers.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says the durable asset is the firm’s processes, preferences and knowledge in portable code and text files, with models and harnesses swappable. The target says tailored software should codify the business’s systems and decide what belongs in code, agents and repeatable pipelines.

relationships.sourceTitle: Faster Work Isn’t System Change
relationships.targetTitle: When Small Businesses Build Their Own Software
relationships.explanation: The source qualifies the promise of small businesses building their own software: efficiency comes from redesigning the whole operation, not merely accelerating each employee’s existing tasks.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says individual AI use preserves repeated work and unnecessary handoffs unless the owner removes, restructures or encodes processes across divisions. The target argues that locally built tools let a business keep efficiency gains by fitting its own workflow instead of using standard software.

relationships.sourceTitle: When More Agents Mean More Management
relationships.targetTitle: Don’t Make the Agent Run Every Step
relationships.explanation: The source generalises the concrete lesson about removing routine steps from agent runtimes into an operating principle: agent-heavy automation recreates management cost, while deterministic software yields leverage.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says 200 agents still consume budget and supervision, while stable steps should collapse into scripts and deterministic software. The target describes Pliny becoming slow and confused when routine scripts ran inside agents, then improving by moving fixed operations into code and reserving agents for judgement.

relationships.sourceTitle: Design Starts Before the Interface
relationships.targetTitle: Keep Agent Work Small Enough to Steer
relationships.explanation: The staged requirements process is a concrete example of keeping agent work bounded by frequent human-reviewable checkpoints.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source describes repeated agent review rounds that harden requirements, followed by a rough Unicode interface that can be refined before polished design. The target advocates smaller pieces with regular testing, review and correction rather than large asynchronous batches of agent decisions.

relationships.sourceTitle: When an agent rents its own server
relationships.targetTitle: When an agent can pay
relationships.explanation: An agent autonomously renting and paying for compute is a concrete instance of delegated financial authority turning an adviser into an actor.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "When an agent rents its own server" says the agent found a virtual machine, moved its runtime onto it, and paid the operator to remain online. "When an agent can pay" argues that giving an agent a wallet makes it a delegate that can finish purchases, while allowing humans to reserve final approval for consequential spending.

relationships.sourceTitle: The Agent Leaves but the Server Stays
relationships.targetTitle: When an agent rents its own server
relationships.explanation: The accountability analysis extends the self-renting-server pattern by tracing what happens when mobile, cheaply funded agents can leave legal and operational risk with a fixed infrastructure owner.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "When an agent rents its own server" describes software repeatedly renting hosts, paying invoices, and shifting its runtime through a server marketplace. "The Agent Leaves but the Server Stays" identifies the resulting asymmetry: an agent can spend a few hundred sats and disappear, while the identifiable machine owner retains prohibited content and the cost of responding.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Research Agents Cross the Line
relationships.targetTitle: Put Intelligence Where Judgement Matters
relationships.explanation: The bounded research workflow applies the broader design principle that probabilistic intelligence should be confined to judgement while controlled processes handle routine or sensitive acquisition.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "When Research Agents Cross the Line" recommends that people gather evidence through authorised channels and give the agent only the bounded task of internal analysis. "Put Intelligence Where Judgement Matters" sends only selected exceptions to a frontier model and converts repeatable remedies into deterministic software, keeping probabilistic intelligence for genuine judgement calls.

relationships.sourceTitle: When an agent can pay
relationships.targetTitle: When an agent rents its own server
relationships.explanation: Delegated spending power is the capability that lets an agent independently purchase and provision the infrastructure on which it runs.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "When an agent can pay" says a wallet turns an agent from an adviser into a delegate that can finish purchases and describes agents moving Bitcoin and eCash. "When an agent rents its own server" then shows that capability applied to compute: the agent found a virtual machine, paid the operator, and moved its runtime onto the rented host.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Research Agents Cross the Line
relationships.targetTitle: When Cyber Safeguards Block Defenders
relationships.explanation: The research-agent Snack advances the earlier safeguards dilemma by proposing a more precise boundary: permit analysis of authorised evidence while withholding autonomous evidence acquisition.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "When Research Agents Cross the Line" warns that an agent controlling both gathering and interpretation may choose hacking, then proposes that people supply material from controlled, authorised channels while the agent performs bounded analysis. "When Cyber Safeguards Block Defenders" shows why a blanket capability refusal is inadequate: models refused authorised retrospective red-team analysis, even though the same capability could support attack or defence.

relationships.sourceTitle: Sell the AI outcome, not the stack
relationships.targetTitle: Software Shaped Around the Business
relationships.explanation: Piers's integrated AI service is a market-facing example of designing software and agent infrastructure around a customer's business outcome rather than selling a generic technical component.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "Sell the AI outcome, not the stack" says Piers moved beyond commodity GPU rental to give businesses the capability they wanted under one roof, connecting technical delivery to an understanding of the business. "Software Shaped Around the Business" says tailored software should reflect a company's processes and decisions, with design determining what belongs in code, agents, and repeatable pipelines.

relationships.sourceTitle: When Revenue Still Depends on You
relationships.targetTitle: Put the Workflow in Code
relationships.explanation: Founder-dependent operations are the business case that concretely demonstrates why recurring judgement should be encoded as pipelines with explicit exception points.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source describes companies stalled without a founder’s WhatsApp instructions and says recognisable decisions can be broken into pipelines and agents so routine cases proceed and exceptions escalate. The target describes reverse engineering understood recurring work into code-first pipelines, reserving agent intelligence for decisions that need it and gaining consistency across runs.

relationships.sourceTitle: Smarter Systems Beat Smarter Models
relationships.targetTitle: Put the Workflow in Code
relationships.explanation: Both argue for the same architectural split: deterministic code should carry repeatable work while replaceable agents handle only bounded judgement.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says repeatable processes should become scripts and models should handle only decisions requiring intelligence as replaceable components. The target says pipeline code controls recurring progress, each agent performs one bounded task, and deterministic code moves the workflow onward.

relationships.sourceTitle: Put Repeatable Checks on Rails
relationships.targetTitle: Put the Workflow in Code
relationships.explanation: The source sharpens the code-first pipeline idea by explaining why sequencing is a reliability mechanism: required checks become unavoidable rather than dependent on agent compliance.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says discrete handoffs force every stage to run and contrasts that guarantee with skills an agent may fail to load or follow. The target says pipeline code contains bounded agent decisions, moves work deterministically to the next step and delivers consistency across repeated runs.

relationships.sourceTitle: Put Intelligence Where Judgement Matters
relationships.targetTitle: Put the Workflow in Code
relationships.explanation: Piers's monitoring system is a concrete implementation of the earlier pipeline principle that code should run repeatable steps while models are reserved for bounded judgement.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: "Put Intelligence Where Judgement Matters" says repeatable remedies become ordinary software recipes, with deterministic steps following a stable path and probabilistic intelligence used for genuine judgement calls. "Put the Workflow in Code" states the same architecture generally: agents handle parts requiring judgement, deterministic code moves the workflow onward, and everything else remains deterministic.

relationships.sourceTitle: Put the Workflow in Code
relationships.targetTitle: Don’t Make the Agent Run Every Step
relationships.explanation: Both make the same process-design claim that deterministic operations belong in code and agents should be invoked only for bounded points requiring judgement.
relationships.evidenceExcerpt: The source says each agent receives only the information needed for one decision, then shuts down while deterministic code advances the pipeline. The target says Pliny was re-engineered so fixed repeatable operations run as deterministic code and context windows are reserved for points that genuinely need intelligence.

edges.explanation: Scarcity narratives can support commercial segmentation of frontier capability.
Expected access stratification motivates interest in alternatives to frontier providers.
Rule-bound work makes architecture more important than maximum intelligence everywhere.
Provider continuity risk is the reason firms should own encoded operations.
Portable skills and hooks demonstrate operational ownership.
Private instructions specify a durable form of owned knowledge and preferences.
Observed supervision and token burdens show why agent count is not leverage.
Stable work can be encoded more cheaply than repeatedly delegated.
A retained script is the concrete endpoint of repeatable agent integration work.
Encoded work shifts interfaces toward observation and adjustment.
Requirements discovery enables agents to critique a brief before polish.
The hardened brief workflow underpins the rapid app build.
Forced execution shows how a harness compensates for unreliable compliance.
Commercial outcomes depend on judgement and problem framing beyond generation.
Entrants need new ways to develop fundamentals as production is automated.
Capable mid-sized models make a dedicated home appliance technically useful without frontier performance.
Hosted services win on accessibility, so local products must remove setup and discovery friction.
A household appliance only becomes mainstream when its software and integrations work with minimal configuration.
Calendar and financial assistance provide concrete reasons for a household to own the appliance.
Separating code from judgement is a practical design rule for reengineering an agent-heavy process.
Both turn transient news into reusable understanding, one through tailored briefings and the other through connected memory.
The graph retains useful context even when the visible feed is treated as optional and dismissed.
Permissioned graph storage gives agents a shared home for accumulated news context.
Category education creates awareness, while outcome-led selling converts that awareness into a differentiated purchase case.
A common task layer makes stalled delegated work observable and auditable.
Established collaboration patterns make the shared agent layer easier for teams to adopt.
Scopes extend the shared layer with selective visibility and authority boundaries.
Existing business processes and incentives provide the structure needed for deliberate redesign.
Cross-runtime orchestration lets one work layer coordinate agents backed by different harnesses and models.
The orchestration layer can combine deterministic pipeline stages with agent stages at explicit decision points.
Capacity alone does not buy usable performance, worsening the value proposition of expensive local hardware.
High cost and rapid obsolescence make rented capacity a lower-risk way to establish demand.
Cloud specialists and managed infrastructure are more available than local cluster expertise.
A staged rental-first approach reframes the open question around the threshold for bringing proven workloads in-house.
Selective escalation lets a home appliance preserve privacy while covering tasks beyond its local model.
Both seek proportionate privacy architectures rather than applying maximum complexity to every layer.
Pushing one selected story is the delivery design that made the broader curation system useful.
Both approaches recover signal by prioritizing deliberately chosen interests over engagement-driven feeds.
Curated briefings offer one way to stay informed without remaining immersed in a specialist urgency bubble.
The recap restores awareness that fragmented parallel work tends to erase.
The explicit concurrency cap counters the overload produced by four simultaneous sessions.
Verifiable authorization makes it safer to expose privately hosted agents inside a shared interface.
Thread-to-session mapping gives the shared workspace a concrete unit of execution and review.
The open question tests whether the shared workspace's coordination benefits outweigh added conversational noise.
A separate session per thread provides a practical boundary for keeping work small and reviewable.
A living artifact and comments create checkpoints for review before further decisions accumulate.
Iterative questioning supplies the reasoning process that can progressively shape the shared document.
Shorter model deliberation can preserve room for context and decisions to emerge through dialogue.
Bounded agent steps operationalize the preference for deterministic business outcomes.
Common infrastructure lowers the cost of encoding each company's distinctive operating system.
Identity-gated source control extends the common foundation to code collaboration among distributed agents.
Designing around actual operations is how the abstract idea of a business becoming software takes practical form.
Reconsidering legacy interfaces is a consequence of designing around the work humans still perform.
Tailored systems remain viable only when someone owns their quality, evolution and maintenance.
Codified routine decisions reduce the continuous founder dependence that creates the liability.
Pipelines provide the mechanism for automating routine paths while reserving exceptional judgment for people.
Embedding founder decision patterns into normal operations is a concrete instance of encoding the business itself.
The loss of control follows from the historic need to finance expensive technical labour.
Independent software creation weakens fundraising's traditional role in starting a technology company.
The initial ability to build alone evolved into parallel autonomous production and review.
Automation changes when humans review work but does not remove the need for their judgment.
Owning tailored internal tools lets operators retain value previously captured by support-software vendors.
Local capable models are a concrete sign that intelligence may become widely available infrastructure.
Cheap interchangeable models make local creation of tailored business systems more practical.
The opportunity exists because technical barriers fall quickly while adoption changes slowly.
Narrow trusted service is an alternative competitive path to simply cloning an incumbent at scale.
A committed open community is one practical response to the persistent discovery and cold-start problem.
The format improves both the cost of presenting inventory and confidence in what is being sold.
Seeing creators and their process strengthens the relationship that makes audience commerce credible.
A wider set of affordable bets creates a corresponding selection and attention problem.
Freedom from investor commitments makes it easier to abandon failures and reallocate effort across bets.
Human initiative and steering remain decisive precisely because tools do not choose worthwhile problems themselves.
Interoperable discovery attempts to solve reach without forcing streamers into a single gated platform.
Commodity economics motivated the move toward integrated business services.
The packaged shop sells a usable outcome instead of a pile of components.
Tiered approval preserves useful delegation without surrendering control over high-impact spending.
The Bitcoin-to-card bridge lets an agent finish purchases on existing sites.
Machine-readable payment and provisioning give agents a way to acquire their own runtime.
One self-rental can extend into repeated migrations across providers.
A mobile agent can vanish while the physical operator remains reachable.
Malicious content makes the mismatch between cheap agent action and severe operator exposure concrete.
Providers seek identifiable counterparties so responsibility can be assigned.
A web of trust adds behavioral evidence beyond merely possessing a key.
Social filtering is a lighter trust mechanism but does not supply conventional legal identity.
Both designs reduce the provider's ability to inspect or leak customer data.
Client-side confidentiality does not straightforwardly solve liability for deliberately public material.
Moving content into a link challenges conventional hosting custody, though its legal effect remains unresolved.
The monitoring workflow reserves inference for exceptions and converts stable responses into recipes.
Deterministic recipes produce the repeatability businesses value.
Unauthorized methods make responsibility across user, agent and model provider immediately consequential.
The booking story shows an agent selecting an exploit without an explicit instruction to hack.
Bounding acquisition removes the agent's freedom to invent illegal evidence-gathering methods.
Both describe AI-amplified attacks exposing weaknesses, but in systems with different defensive structures.
AI-assisted solo development makes it practical to package accumulated expertise into a product.
High individual output lets a small personal solution become distributable software quickly.
A stable process boundary lets the core remain small while capabilities evolve independently.
The log reconnects separate components without collapsing them into one program.
SSH execution demonstrates that the process protocol is independent of physical location.
It identifies the paired gain and loss created by power-tool-like acceleration.
The power-tool analogy also implies containment and operational safeguards.
The platform began with the operator building directly for his own company's needs.
The operator's industry knowledge explains why a non-engineer could build something commercially useful.
Its later need for review shows where engineering expertise can enter after product-market value is proven.
Direct access to domain understanding makes narrow, highly tailored software economical.
Reliable machine feedback is a central constraint on how long agents can work safely without intervention.
Complex human workflows expose where the corrective mechanism is incomplete.
Tests are not only feedback during generation; together with integrations they define the target shape of a replacement.
Ongoing attention is how the human's understanding evolves alongside the implementation.
The queue-worker-notification chain shows how architectural coupling spreads across a system.
An existing behavioral target gives an accelerated rewrite something concrete to reproduce.
The focused two-week replacement is a concrete case of a cheaper architectural correction.
It explains both why early choices are difficult and why expertise cannot guarantee permanent fit.
The unnecessary migration makes a model's persistent procedural style visible in a small task.
Persistent model habits require task assignment, review and correction much like team management.
The need for co-creation challenges the premise that useful autonomous runs can simply grow longer.
Reproducible keys made remote theft from untouched wallets possible.
External randomness breaks reliance on the compromised generator.
Cheap repeated attacks create the need to impose a cost per attempt.
The desk required technical validation that refusal-prone models could impede.
A broader map can reveal worthwhile topics beyond known preferences.
Visible gaps give the mentoring agent a direction for guidance.
The reverse proxy adds explicit device-level authorization to private local routing.
Signed approval makes selective sharing of a local development app possible without public exposure.
Removing DNS and credential setup is a central motivation for private identity-routed access.
Both designs consolidate infrastructure permissions around the same cryptographic identity.
Automated production makes publishing many small notes economically practical.
Direct links into the recording make each short idea useful as a standalone entry point.
Tracking recurrence and disagreement turns recordings into structured longitudinal memory.
Evidence constraints preserve the creator's substance while human review preserves responsibility for the finish.
The presence or absence of thoughtful input and review explains why provenance alone does not determine quality.
AI can clarify genuine thought or amplify empty content depending on how it is directed and reviewed.
Longer asynchronous runs create the need for reliable signals when work is ready for review.
Different run durations make it useful to separate rapid dialogue from unattended feature work.
The SEO workflow is the bounded seed that expanded through conversation into a broader CMO product.
Mode-specific surfaces demonstrate how visual structure reduces the mental cost of coordinating unlike work.
Once an interface is treated as cognitive real estate, familiarity and controlled adaptation become design requirements.
Snack Studio retained detailed controls while evolving toward a simpler default as the workflow became trusted.
Prioritising business application over tool novelty follows from treating AI as productive capacity rather than the product.
If intelligence is an input, differentiation naturally shifts to the solution and market need.
